analysis: Only docs/provider/cli-reference.md changed, in three places. (1) The 'Last updated' date moved to 2026-10-23. (2) Line 52 now says inline GLM video input (data:video/mp4 or quicktime) works at constant or variable frame rate, sampled at 2 FPS and decoded target-only. This is documentation only. The decoding code, and whether the inline-video temp-file mitigation from T-050 still applies to the VFR path, are not in the supplied evidence. (3) A new row at head line ~1578 documents ~/.darkbloom/verified-weights.json (0600, env DARKBLOOM_VERIFIED_WEIGHTS_FILE). It holds managed GLM load hashes bound to file identities and reused for startup registration. That row is only in the patch excerpt, not in the supplied base units 1-821. The documented behavior touches the weight-integrity assets and threats A-004, T-012 and T-027. A reused, file-identity-bound cached hash could be stale or spoofable if the identity binding is weak (for example size/mtime only), since the operator controls the weights directory. That would only widen the existing operator-replaces-weights concern (ADV-001); the coordinator-side hash check is not shown to be affected. The base text already describes hash reuse for unchanged snapshots (lines 320-325), and VerifiedWeightHashStore.swift is not supplied. I found no concrete security regression in the docs-only change. Questions for later passes: what identity fields bind a cached hash; whether the file is owner-only and tamper-resistant; whether mandatory fresh checks remain for registration and SSD loads; and whether VFR video decoding keeps the no-plaintext-temp-file property. No claims about the code are made here.
